title: Check if a Parentheses String Can Be Valid
summary: Given a parentheses string s and a binary string locked of the same length, determine if s can be transformed into a valid parentheses string by changing characters in s where locked is '0', while keeping characters where locked is '1' unchanged.
statement: Given a parentheses string s and a binary string locked of the same length, determine if s can be transformed into a valid parentheses string by changing characters in s where locked is '0', while keeping characters where locked is '1' unchanged. Return true if possible, otherwise false.
constraints: s and locked have equal length; locked zero positions may change to either parenthesis while locked one positions stay fixed.
A valid result has balanced totals and no prefix with more closing than opening parentheses.
Return whether some allowed replacement is valid.
reference_solution:
def can_make_valid_parentheses(s,locked):
    if len(s)%2:return False
    possible=0
    for char,fixed in zip(s,locked):
        if char=='(' or fixed=='0':possible+=1
        elif possible:possible-=1
        else:return False
    possible=0
    for char,fixed in zip(reversed(s),reversed(locked)):
        if char==')' or fixed=='0':possible+=1
        elif possible:possible-=1
        else:return False
    return True

hints: A forward scan must be able to cover every locked close; a reverse scan must be able to cover every locked open.
Treat each unlocked character optimistically as an opening in the forward scan and as a closing in reverse.
Reject odd length or either scan whose available balance would go negative.
Both directional feasibility conditions plus even length are necessary and sufficient to assign flexible positions into a globally valid sequence.
